manuscript_meta.title: LATENT SEQUENCE DECOMPOSITIONS William Chan∗ Carnegie Mellon University williamchan@cmu.edu

report.summary: This paper introduces Latent Sequence Decompositions (LSD), a novel framework for sequence-to-sequence models where the tokenization of the output sequence is not fixed but learned as a latent variable. The model learns a distribution over possible decompositions (e.g., into characters or multi-character word pieces) that is conditioned on both the input and output sequences. The authors propose a training method based on left-to-right sampling with an ε-greedy strategy to manage the intractable search space of all possible decompositions. They apply LSD to the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) speech recognition task, demonstrating a significant Word Error Rate (WER) reduction from 14.8% (character baseline) to 12.9%, and further to 9.6% when combined with a convolutional encoder, outperforming previous end-to-end models at the time of publication.

points: The core idea of treating sequence decomposition as a latent variable conditioned on the input is highly original. It moves beyond the prevailing paradigm of using fixed, pre-determined tokenization schemes (characters, words, or static word pieces).

The work addresses a fundamentally important problem in sequence modeling. Suboptimal tokenization can limit model performance, increase computational cost, and struggle with rare or out-of-vocabulary words. LSD provides a flexible and data-driven solution.
The experimental results are strong and convincing. The LSD model achieves a 12.7% relative WER improvement over a competitive character-level baseline on the WSJ task (12.9% vs. 14.8%).

When combined with a CNN encoder, the proposed model achieves a state-of-the-art result (at the time) of 9.6% WER without an external language model, demonstrating the method's effectiveness and its compatibility with other architectural improvements.

The comparison against the 'Maximum Extension' (MaxExt) baseline is very effective for demonstrating that simply using longer tokens is not sufficient, which strongly supports the need for learning the decomposition dynamically.
The paper is exceptionally well-written. The motivation is clearly articulated, the mathematical framework is presented formally, and the model architecture is described in sufficient detail.
Figure 1 provides a clear and insightful analysis of the learned decompositions, showing that the model learns to use a mix of token lengths, which supports the central hypothesis of the paper.

The training procedure relies on a heuristic approximation (left-to-right sampling with an ε-greedy strategy) to sample from the posterior p(z|y, x; θ). The authors acknowledge this is a biased procedure. While the results are strong, the theoretical justification for why this approximation works well could be strengthened.

The paper notes that without the ε-greedy strategy, the model collapses to a local minimum of using single characters. This suggests the training dynamics are sensitive and potentially unstable, which could be a practical limitation.

detailed_comments.comment: An automated check of the bibliography flagged that one reference could not be resolved by the tool because it lacked a DOI or other machine-readable metadata. The evidence pack notes this does not mean the reference is invalid, but it does hinder discoverability. Please review your reference list to ensure all entries are complete and formatted with sufficient metadata (e.g., DOI, full title, venue) to be resolvable by standard indexing tools.

The use of an ε-greedy sampling strategy is a pragmatic solution to avoid local minima. However, it would be beneficial to provide more analysis on this choice. For instance, how sensitive is the final performance to the annealing schedule of ε? Is there a risk that this exploration encourages suboptimal decompositions early on that the model cannot recover from later?

The comparison against the 'Maximum Extension' (MaxExt) baseline is very effective for demonstrating that simply using longer tokens is not sufficient. The fact that all MaxExt models underperform the character baseline is a strong piece of evidence for the necessity of learning the decomposition dynamically.

questions: What is the computational overhead (in terms of training time and inference latency) of the LSD framework compared to the character-level baseline, given the need to sample decompositions during training and perform a search over a larger token vocabulary during decoding?

The vocabulary of word pieces was created from n-gram character counts from the training set. Have you explored other methods for generating the initial token vocabulary Z, and how sensitive is the model's performance to this initial choice?

The appendix shows that the LSD model can generate multiple decompositions for the same word sequence. Could you provide some analysis on the diversity of these decompositions and whether they correlate with input characteristics, such as speaking rate or accent, as hypothesized in the introduction?
report.overall_assessment:
This is a strong and impactful paper that introduces LSD, a novel and effective framework for learning dynamic tokenizations in sequence-to-sequence models. The core idea is original, the problem it addresses is significant, and the empirical results on the WSJ ASR task are impressive, showing substantial improvements over a strong baseline. The paper is exceptionally well-written and the experiments are thoughtfully designed.

The only minor weakness is the reliance on a heuristic training procedure, which the authors are transparent about. The reviewers have raised several excellent questions regarding computational overhead, vocabulary sensitivity, and the diversity of learned decompositions, which would further strengthen the paper if addressed. A minor bibliographic issue was also noted where a reference was not machine-readable, which should be an easy fix. Overall, this is a high-quality contribution that requires only minor revisions to be ready for publication.

This paper introduces Latent Sequence Decompositions (LSD), a novel framework for sequence-to-sequence models where the tokenization of the output sequence is not fixed but learned as a latent variable. findings.title: Ölçüm Araçları ve Operasyonelleştirme Açıklığı
findings.summary: Makale, konuşma tanıma görevinde standart bir metrik olan Kelime Hata Oranı (WER) kullanmaktadır. Bu metrik, alanda yaygın olarak kabul görmüş ve operasyonelleştirilmesi açık bir ölçümdür. Ayrıca, giriş özellikleri (80 boyutlu filtre bankaları) ve model mimarisi (BLSTM, LSTM, MLP) detaylı bir şekilde açıklanmıştır.

manuscript_anchors.quote: Our LSD model achieves 12.9% WER compared to a character baseline of 14.8% WER.

Our input features were 80 dimensional ﬁlterbanks computed every 10ms with delta and delta-delta acceleration normalized with per speaker mean and variance as generated by Kaldi (Povey et al., 2011). The EncodeRNN function is a 3 layer BLSTM with 256 LSTM units per-direction (or 512 total) and 4 = 22 time factor reduction. The DecodeRNN is a 1 layer LSTM with 256 LSTM units.

Bu tür modellerde, genellikle istatistiksel varsayım testleri yerine modelin performans metrikleri üzerinden karşılaştırmalar yapılır. Kullanılan optimizasyon algoritması (ADAM) ve eğitim stratejileri (gradient norm clipping, gaussian weight noise, L2 weight decay, epsilon-greedy keşif) alana uygun ve iyi tanımlanmıştır.

manuscript_anchors.quote: We used ADAM with the default hyperparameters described in (Kingma & Ba, 2015), however we decayed the learning rate from 1e−3 to 1e−4. We used 8 GPU workers for asynchronous SGD under the TensorFlow framework (Abadi et al., 2015). We monitor the dev93 Word Error Rate (WER) until convergence and report the corresponding eval92 WER.

In practice, we ﬁnd that the when the model is trained with this method, it quickly collapses to using single character targets, and never escapes from this local minima1. Thus, we fol-low an ϵ-greedy exploration strategy commonly found in reinforcement learning literature (Sutton & Barto, 1998) – we sample zt from a mixture of a uniform distribution over valid next tokens and p (zt|x, y, z<t, θ).

WER) üzerinden yapılır ve geleneksel istatistiksel test varsayımları bu bağlamda doğrudan uygulanmaz. Kullanılan optimizasyon ve eğitim teknikleri, bu alandaki en iyi uygulamalarla uyumludur.

findings.title: Makale Konusu ve Hedef Track Uyumu
findings.summary: Makale, 'Latent Sequence Decompositions' (Gizli Dizi Ayrıştırmaları) çerçevesini sunarak, dizilerin belirgin bir şekilde sabit token'lara ayrıştırılması yerine, model eğitimi sırasında bu ayrıştırmaların öğrenilmesini öneriyor. Bu yaklaşım, özellikle konuşma tanıma gibi alanlarda, girdi ve çıktı dizilerine bağlı olarak dinamik token ayrıştırmalarının önemini vurguluyor. manuscript_anchors.quote: In this paper we present Latent Sequence Decompositions (LSD), a framework in which the decomposition of sequences into constituent tokens is learnt during the training of the model. The decomposition depends both on the input sequence and on the output sequence.

We argue against using ﬁxed deterministic decompositions of a sequence that has been deﬁned a priori. Word segmented models (Luong et al., 2015; Jean et al., 2015) often have to deal with large softmax sizes, rare words and Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) words. Character models (Chan et al., 2016; Bahdanau et al., 2016a) overcome the OOV problem by modelling the smallest output unit, however this typically results in long decoder lengths and computationally expensive inference.

action_plan.acceptance_check: Örneklem büyüklüğü gerekçesi veya güç analizi eksikliğine dair açıklama metne eklenmiş olmalı.

action_plan.instruction: Raporlanan WER değerleri için güven aralıkları veya standart hatalar gibi belirsizlik ölçüleri eklenmelidir. Bu, gözlemlenen iyileşmelerin istatistiksel olarak ne kadar güvenilir olduğunu anlamak için kritik öneme sahiptir.
action_plan.acceptance_check: Tüm ana WER sonuçları için güven aralıkları veya standart hatalar raporlanmış olmalı.

action_plan.instruction: Makalede kullanılan kod tabanına (örn. GitHub deposu) ve/veya özel veri setlerine (eğer varsa) erişim sağlayan bir bağlantı eklenmelidir. Eğer veri setleri kamuya açık değilse, erişim koşulları veya benzer veri setlerine yönlendirme yapılmalıdır.
action_plan.acceptance_check: Makalede kod ve/veya veri setlerine erişim sağlayan geçerli bir URL veya açıklama bulunmalıdır.

action_plan.instruction: Denklem 7'nin neden 'unbiased estimator' olduğunu daha detaylı açıklayın veya ilgili bir referans ekleyin. Bu, okuyucuların türetmenin geçerliliğini daha iyi anlamasına yardımcı olacaktır.
action_plan.acceptance_check: Unbiased estimator açıklaması veya referansı eklenmiş mi?

action_plan.instruction: Ana sonuçlar olan WER değerleri için güven aralıkları veya standart hatalar gibi belirsizlik ölçüleri eklenmelidir. Bu, sonuçların istatistiksel sağlamlığını daha iyi yansıtacaktır.
action_plan.acceptance_check: Ana WER sonuçları belirsizlik ölçüleriyle birlikte raporlanmış olmalı.
